issues.legal_issue: An amendment increasing the retirement age of government servants applies to employees of a statutory corporation whose service regulations make government service rules applicable, unless the corporation validly amends those regulations.
material_facts: The employees had transferred from a government department to the corporation under legislation that preserved their existing service conditions until altered by the corporation.
The corporation’s service regulation provided that government rules, regulations and orders governing service conditions applied equally to its employees.
The government increased its employees’ retirement age, but the corporation did not amend its service regulation to prescribe a different retirement age.
The corporation relied on a government policy direction and its own administrative decision to retire its employees at the earlier age.
The employees challenged their retirement orders in appeals and writ petitions.
issues.conclusion: The increased retirement age applicable to government servants also applied to the corporation’s employees because the corporation had not amended its service regulation. A different retirement age could be prescribed only by amending that regulation with the government’s prior approval; any such amendment would operate prospectively.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 37 and 97(2)(c) of the Uttar Pradesh Water Supply and Sewerage Act, 1975, transferred employees retain their service conditions until altered by the corporation, and the corporation may regulate service conditions with the State Government’s prior approval. Regulation 31 incorporated the rules, regulations and orders applicable to government servants, including later amendments, because it did not limit incorporation to rules existing when the regulation was made. The corporation’s general power under Section 15(1), and policy directions under Section 89, could not override a regulation made under the specific regulation-making power. Under V.T. Khanzode v. Reserve Bank of India, a statutory corporation may act only within the powers conferred expressly or by necessary implication; general administrative directions may govern service conditions where relevant regulations have not been made, but cannot displace existing regulations.

predicates.service_retirement_dispute: Employees of a statutory corporation challenged decisions about their retirement age in an appeal or writ proceeding.
predicates.regulation_makes_government_service_rule: The corporation had made a service regulation providing that government service rules and orders applied to its employees.
predicates.government_retirement_age_was_increased: The government increased the retirement age applicable to its own employees.
predicates.corporation_did_not_amend_service_regula: The corporation had not amended its service regulation to prescribe a different retirement age.

issues.definition: When employees challenge a retirement decision, an increased government retirement age applies to corporation employees if their service regulation incorporates government service rules and the corporation has not amended that regulation.

issues.legal_issue: Employees who continued working beyond the earlier retirement age under an interim order are not required to repay salary received for that continued service.
material_facts: The retirement orders were challenged in appeals and writ petitions.
Some employees were permitted by interim orders to continue working up to the applicable retirement age.
The Court set aside the orders directing retirement at the earlier age.
issues.conclusion: No recovery is to be made from employees who were allowed to continue working up to the applicable retirement age under an interim order.
issues.legal_principle: The Court expressly directed that salary paid to employees who continued working by virtue of interim orders should not be recovered. No earlier case or statutory provision was relied on for this direction.

predicates.service_retirement_dispute: Employees of a statutory corporation challenged decisions about their retirement age in an appeal or writ proceeding.
predicates.employee_continued_working_under_interim: An interim order allowed an employee to continue working after the corporation had directed retirement.
predicates.employee_reached_applicable_retirement_a: The employee continued working until the retirement age applicable to that employee.

issues.definition: Salary is not recoverable when an employee challenging a retirement decision continued working under an interim order until the applicable retirement age.

issues.legal_issue: Employees prematurely retired through an erroneous decision, through no fault of their own, are entitled to salary for the unserved portion of their employment up to the applicable retirement age.
material_facts: The retirement orders were challenged in appeals and writ petitions.
Some employees were not permitted to continue working after the earlier retirement age because of the corporation’s decision.
The Court found that the corporation had erroneously decided that those employees had to retire at the earlier age.
The employees were not at fault for being prevented from continuing to work.
issues.conclusion: Employees who were not permitted to continue working because of the corporation’s erroneous decision, through no fault of their own, are entitled to salary for the remaining period up to the applicable retirement age; the corporation was directed to pay it within three months of receiving the order.
issues.legal_principle: The Court directed payment of salary for the remaining period because employees had been prevented from continuing to work by the corporation’s erroneous decision and were not at fault. No earlier case or statutory provision was relied on for this direction.

predicates.service_retirement_dispute: Employees of a statutory corporation challenged decisions about their retirement age in an appeal or writ proceeding.
predicates.employee_was_prevented_from_continuing_w: The corporation did not allow an employee to continue working after the retirement age it had applied.
predicates.corporation_retirement_decision_was_erro: The corporation’s decision to retire the employee before the applicable retirement age was erroneous.
predicates.employee_was_not_at_fault: The employee was not responsible for being prevented from continuing to work.

issues.definition: An employee challenging a retirement decision is entitled to salary for the remainder of the employment period up to the applicable retirement age if an erroneous decision prevented continued work and the employee was not at fault.
